key_insight: Variational circuits can look increasingly random by common complexity diagnostics without losing trainability, showing that statistical complexity and optimization difficulty are not the same thing.
engineering_relevance: For quantum algorithm design, this means deeper or more expressive ansätze may still be practical if locality preserves usable gradients, even when state statistics resemble random-matrix behavior.
method: Studied structured variational circuits on the 1D cluster-Ising model and a generalized toric code Hamiltonian.
Tracked complexity using Porter-Thomas statistics, entanglement-spectrum level statistics, and inverse participation ratios.
Compared these diagnostics against variational optimization behavior and gradient scaling across circuit depth.
evidence_signal: As depth increased, the circuits approached random-state-like and random-matrix-like signatures while optimization remained effective, with no observed exponential gradient suppression in the studied regime.
watch_item: The results are limited to finite-depth, structured circuits and the specific models tested, so deeper or less local architectures may still encounter barren plateaus.
paper_title: Separation of Statistical Complexity and Trainability in Variational Quantum Circuits
